clue.text: Not there? Can get in when sober

indicators.note: to get in is to enter, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: someone not there is absent
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A question about why someone stays away, joined to an invitation to come in once they've sobered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not there?' reads as a question but supplies the outer letters; 'Can' is a container, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from alcohol, so is a synonym for someone staying sober.

clue.text: Asbo let university work with no limits

indicators.note: to work material is to shape it into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university allowing an Asbo to be served without restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British antisocial behaviour order, a court order restricting someone's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means total and unrestricted, as in absolute power.

clue.text: Loses control of second lot of children

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
kids are children

explanation.surface: A parent losing their grip on a second batch of offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that skids slides out of the driver's command, so it loses control.

clue.text: "My liege, repeat it all in a fashion that''s unlawful?"

definitions.note: the answer is an adverb; the whole phrase 'in a fashion that's unlawful' gives its sense

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reworked into another form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the word it said twice
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A courtier asks the monarch whether everything must be done again unlawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeat' tells you to write 'it' twice before shuffling everything together.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegitimately means in a way contrary to law or rules, i.e. in an illegal manner.

clue.text: One hundred and fifty in body of church after start of evensong in, for example, the Vatican

indicators.note: start asks for only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: opening letter of evensong

indicators.note: something placed in a body sits inside it

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
C is 100 and L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Church imagery: a crowd of 150 in the nave of St Peter's after evensong.
explanation.walkthrough: The nave is the main body of a church; the final 'in' simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly surrounded by another state, as Vatican City lies within Rome.

clue.text: Dramatic scene when, in Paris, the water is added to the bill

parts.note: a tab is a bill
l'eau is French for the water

explanation.surface: A diner in Paris sees bottled water added to the bill and makes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' signals a French word; 'the water' in French is l'eau, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking group or scene, as in a tableau vivant of motionless actors.

clue.text: Might it goad singular football team into action?

definitions.text: Might it goad singular football team into action?

indicators.note: making a plural name singular strips its final plural ending

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: Wondering whether something could stir a lacklustre football side into action.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a north London football club; make the name singular and you have the whole answer, which is also what the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a rider's spiked heel device used to urge a horse on, hence anything that goads into action.

clue.text: Depiction of beam in doorway

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: a portal is a doorway
a beam of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A painting showing a sunbeam falling across a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a representation of someone or something, in art or acting.

clue.text: Negligent in the matter of a girl

parts.note: re means concerning
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone careless where a young woman is concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means careless in one's duty, a straight synonym for being negligent.

clue.text: Garishly romanticised college attended by poor Colin and our boy

parts.note: a tech is a technical college

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A rose-tinted account of a college shared by unlucky Colin and the family's son.
explanation.definitionFit: Technicoloured, from the vivid film process, describes something vividly coloured or glamorised beyond reality.

clue.text: Not moving yet

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like something not yet moving; it is two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for being stationary and an adverb meaning up to now or nevertheless.

clue.text: First consultant, skilful on weight of wire

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: opening letter of consultant
skilful means able
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A senior, capable consultant weighing in on wiring, perhaps an electrician's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wire' is the old informal word for a telegram, not a metal strand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cablegram is a telegram sent by undersea cable, and to send a telegram was informally to wire.

clue.text: Dish Alan cooked around sink

indicators.note: around says one set of letters surrounds another
cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to sink is to sag

explanation.surface: Alan prepares a dish standing at the kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is the Italian baked pasta dish of layered sheets, sauce and cheese.

clue.text: Urges others in organisation to hold a vote

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside
putting letters into an organisation means arranging them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Someone presses colleagues in their organisation to hold a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to encourage earnestly, a close synonym for pressing someone to act.

clue.text: High safety precautions against terrorists, for example

parts.note: high and tight are both slang for drunk
safety is security

explanation.surface: Elevated safety measures put in place against terrorist threats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High safety' reads as one phrase about raised measures, but high is slang for drunk, as is tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight security means strict protective measures, such as those deployed when terrorism is feared.

clue.text: Snail can do ports a good turn

indicators.note: a turn swings round to face backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
a can holds things inside it, so the letters are contained within the next words

parts.note: the run of letters sits across these words, ending inside good

explanation.surface: A snail doing harbours a good turn, absurd as that sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are already there, running backwards through 'do ports a good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastropods are the class of molluscs that includes snails and slugs, so a snail is an example.

clue.text: Duck? I object to endless correspondence on something to eat

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
I as the object of a verb is me
a letter is correspondence

explanation.surface: Someone protesting about a duck, then about mail, and finally getting a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' looks like a protest but is grammar: I as an object becomes ME. A duck is a cricketer's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a dish of beaten eggs fried in a pan, one example of food.

clue.text: Trouble over medicinal plant? It's easily solved

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb
trouble is a problem

explanation.surface: Fretting over a sickly herb, then being told the issue is an easy fix.
explanation.walkthrough: A simple is an archaic name for a herb used in medicine; 'over' just places Trouble after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple problem is one with an obvious, effortless answer, so it is quickly solved.

clue.text: Paying regularly for a moral lapse during part of the race

indicators.note: during means within a span, so one part sits inside another

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a race
a sin is a moral lapse

explanation.surface: A runner pays a price for a moral slip made partway through a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasing something means renting it through regular payments rather than buying it outright.

clue.text: Quiet country has almost produced a swimmer

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, quietly
Iran is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peaceful nation has turned out a top swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests an athlete, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A piranha is a sharp-toothed South American freshwater fish, so it is something that swims.

clue.text: A black horse for a highwayman — and his sister?

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Black Bess was the horse of the highwayman Dick Turpin

explanation.surface: A highwayman's black horse, and then a joke about his sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was a famous 18th-century English highwayman whose horse was Black Bess; 'A black horse' tempts you to take all of BLACK BESS, but only B is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess heads a convent of nuns, who are addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Cap rate? Bit of a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Assessing a hat and finding it a bit of a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap with ridges worn by Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Hall nearly replete, having all the people it can hold

definitions.text: all the people it can hold

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hall is a room
replete means full

explanation.surface: A hall almost full, with everyone it can accommodate inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomful is the quantity or number of people that fills a room.

clue.text: Paper on return of oil supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A document about the return on an oil supply deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a reversal signal, but reversing 'of oil' does not work; the five letters must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet of paper folded once, or a single leaf of a book or manuscript.

clue.text: Being outclassed?

parts.note: surface reading: being beaten by a superior opponent
setter's reading: being put out of the class, as when a pupil is thrown out of school

explanation.walkthrough: Outclassed normally means beaten by someone better; read literally it is being sent out of class.
explanation.definitionFit: Being expelled from school is being removed from one's class, a literal reading of outclassed.

clue.text: Allow soldiers at the front to find other tenants

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to allow is to let

explanation.surface: Permitting troops on the front line to look for somebody else.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) go at the front of LET.
explanation.definitionFit: To relet a property is to rent it out again, which means finding new occupants.

clue.text: In this way daughter gets a drink

parts.note: so means in this way
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent describing how their daughter gets something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty: it supplies the final A and also sits with 'drink' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink or soda water.

clue.text: Imposing design — or a mess?

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether an ambitious design is impressive or just a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means impressive and imposing in scale, often pretentiously so.
